tender.title: J5 Resources to deliver EWMP User Case 1 - Additional effort
tender.description:
The contract award is required to support the delivery of Phase 1 of the project following the introduction of additional scope and functionality requirements. The expanded scope necessitates additional development time and specialist consultancy support to design, configure, and implement the required enhancements.
Due to the ongoing agile and evolving nature of the Phase 1 programme, it has been determined that the continued engagement of two Hexagon consultants is necessary to ensure the successful completion of Phase 1 within the planned delivery timescales.
The work involves the configuration and modification of the existing installed J5 application. As Hexagon is the incumbent provider and support organisation for the live J5 environment, its consultants possess the specialist knowledge and technical expertise required to make the necessary adjustments while minimising risk to operational systems and avoiding disruption to currently live applications.
Continued access to Hexagon consultancy capability is therefore essential to support the configuration, customisation, stabilisation, and optimisation of the application, ensuring the successful delivery of Phase 1 and the realisation of the required business outcomes.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
Sellafield Ltd has completed a study and determined that the new PCM Tracking Application should be developed using its existing, on-premise Hexagon J5 platform. Hexagon has previously developed multiple J5 applications for Sellafield Ltd and is the incumbent supplier responsible for supporting the shared J5 environment.
The requirement is for the configuration and enhancement of Sellafield's existing installed J5 application. Due to the technical complexity of the live environment and the need to ensure compatibility with existing applications, the work can only be undertaken by suitably authorised and experienced Hexagon consultants with specialist knowledge of the J5 platform and Sellafield's current implementation.
Awarding this work to an alternative supplier would introduce significant technical risk, including potential impacts to live operational applications, increased integration and mobilisation costs, and delays to the delivery of Phase 1. The requirement therefore constitutes additional repeat work and is justified on technical grounds, as Hexagon is uniquely positioned to safely configure and modify the existing environment without compromising business continuity.
This requirement is limited in scope and duration and represents a controlled, time-bound engagement to complete Phase 1 of the PCM Tracking Application while Sellafield Ltd considers its longer-term capability and sourcing strategy.

tender.description: Procurement of a bespoke and sterile Biosafety cabinet. University of Edinburgh believes Erlab is the only supplier capable of meeting the University's specialist requirement

lots.description: The Edinburgh Genome Foundry (EGF) is a unique facility specialising in the generation of large numbers of genetic constructs to equip cells with new or improved functionality. Currently, the facility is undergoing major expansion to incorporate a fully automated, fully-enclosed platform for the automated handling of mammalian cells. As part of this research the University is looking to procure a bespoke, adaptable and sterile biosafety cabinet which needs to fit into a height restricted space (2.5m maximum ceiling height). 100% fresh air intake solution with no re-circulation is required in the room to prevent heat, humidity and gas build-up inside the cabinet in order to prevent contamination. The University also has a limited budget and requires the cabinet to be installed without any costly building modifications such as ducting and the ability to be modified in the future in response to changing facility demand. The University intends to award the contract to Erlab who are able to fully meet the University’s specification and budget.

procurementMethodRationaleClassification.description: The procurement falls outside the scope of application of the directive

tender.procurementMethodRationale: Following detailed technical engagement with the suppliers identified as potentially capable of meeting Edinburgh Genome Foundry’s requirement, it was established that Erlab is the only supplier able to provide a compliant solution that satisfies all of the University's essential technical, operational and financial requirements. Erlab will provide a fully bespoke and highly configurable enclosure that can be adapted both to the current automated platform and to future expansion requirements. The proposed solution will fit into the limited space available, with an overall height of just under 2.5m, which it achieves by eliminating the need for top mounted air intakes or exhaust systems. This reduces the need for costly building modifications or ductwork installation. The system has 0% air recirculation, drawing air from surrounding environment and exhausts filtered air directly into the room, which reduces the need for external ducting. 100% fresh air intake solution with no re-circulation is required in the room to prevent heat, humidity and gas build-up inside the cabinet in order to prevent contamination.

tender.title: Coding NDNS Consumption data into EFSA’s food classification+description -FoodEx
tender.description:
As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to.  
To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS).  The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. 
Tenders are invited to carry out the recoding of NDNS consumption data to FoodEx2, a standardised system for classifying and describing food.

tender.title: Economic impact assessment for an outbreak of African swine fever in the UK
tender.description:
AHDB is seeking quotes for an economic impact assessment for an outbreak of African swine fever (ASF) in the UK.  This project forms part of a wider area of work concerned with preparing the UK pig and pork industry for a potential outbreak.
ASF is a viral disease of pigs which is well-established in parts of Europe, Asia and Africa, with a reservoir of infection in the wild boar population.  It is transmitted through infected pigs and contaminated pork products.  ASF represents a significant and growing threat to the UK pig and pork sector, primarily from the potential introduction of the disease, particularly via illegally imported pork and pork products entering the country through passenger routes and other uncontrolled channels.
AHDB has been working alongside other industry stakeholders and partners over the last several years on ASF prevention and awareness.  We are now working to prepare the industry so that it can continue to function as normally as possible should an outbreak occur and recover rapidly thereafter.
In addition to quantifying the economic and productivity impacts of a potential ASF outbreak in the UK, this review is intended to serve as an evidence base for industry representative bodies (e.g. National Pig Association, British Meat Processors' Association, National Farmers' Union) in their engagement with Government and other stakeholders.
A key objective is to evidence the scale of economic risk posed to the UK pig sector and wider agri-food supply chain.
As part of this wider area of work, and in light of the outbreak of ASF in Spain in November 2025, AHDB is looking to update and build on two previous economic impact assessments which it produced in 2018 and 2020.
Estimated value is approx £40k.

tender.description:
Cardiff Council is preparing to recommission Young Persons Accommodation and Support Services and is issuing this notice to update the market on its intentions for the forthcoming procurement. Consultation and engagement activity has already informed the proposed service model, and the purpose of this notice is to provide potential bidders with advance information on the anticipated contract Lots, values, timetable and market event arrangements.
Background and Purpose
The Council is seeking to recommission an integrated model of housing-related support for young people aged 16 to 24 who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or moving on from care. The proposed model is intended to strengthen prevention, improve pathway flow, provide flexible accommodation and support options, and respond to increasing levels of complexity and need among young people.
The future services will support the Council’s statutory duties under relevant housing and social care legislation and will align with Cardiff’s Housing Support Programme Strategy, Corporate Parenting Strategy and wider commitments to preventing homelessness and improving outcomes for vulnerable young people.
Proposed Contract Lots
The Council anticipates tendering three separate contract Lots:
Lot 1 - Advice and Prevention, including early intervention, mediation and family support, and recruitment and management of supported lodgings placements.	Approx. £350,000 per annum
(includes payments to those offering supported lodgings placements).
Lot 2 - Supported Accommodation for young people within identified provision, flexible support for young people with varying levels of need and provision of move-on floating support.
Approx. 110 units of accommodation; mix of hostels, smaller houses of multiple occupancy, dispersed provision and housing first. Approx. £2,900,000 per annum

The values stated above are indicative and subject to final approval, confirmation of available funding, affordability within approved budgets and the final procurement documentation. 
Management of Accommodation 
For Lots 2 and 3, the Council is commissioning the support element only. The Council will provide a property schedule with the tender documentation, setting out the accommodation provision available for use. Successful tenderers will be responsible for entering into the necessary agreements with landlords for those properties and for delivering associated housing management duties. This will include setting rental charges and claiming the appropriate rental income, where applicable, to offset eligible housing management and accommodation-related costs.
Contract Duration

tender.title: CCS061 Framework for Alternative Education Provision in Derbyshire
tender.description:
Derbyshire County Council is seeking to establish an open framework of Alternative Provision for Children and Young People (CYP) in Derbyshire who are excluded, at risk of being excluded, disengaged or require alternative educational arrangements to meet their needs.
The Framework will deliver education provision that supports CYPs to prepare them for the next stages of education, learning or adult life (including where relevant improving behaviour and attendance prior to re-integration into school) in line with the four approaches set out below:
(a) Preventative support in mainstream schools to help at risk CYPs to remain in mainstream education.
(b) Time-limited short-term placements to address and meet pupil's needs with the expectation to remain in or return to mainstream schools.
(c) Transitional placements for CYPs who need support prior to moving on to next stages of learning, education, training, or entry into the workforce and/or the next stages of their lives.
(d) Placements for Children who have been permanently excluded (where applicable).
The services to be provided through the Framework have been split into 5 Lots:
• Lot A: Preventative & Early Intervention
• Lot B: Targeted Short-Term Provision
• Lot C: Specialist Long-Term Provision
• Lot D: Primary AP & Transition Support
• Lot E: Vocational & Progression Pathways

lots.title: Lot A - Preventative & Early Intervention
lots.description:
To provide short-term, structured interventions that prevent escalation of need and support pupils to remain engaged in mainstream education. This Lot focuses on early intervention for CYP in KS1 through to KS4, and post 16 who are at risk of disengagement due to low-level SEMH needs or Emotionally Based School Avoidance (EBSA). The provision is aimed at:
(a)	Preventing escalation to higher-tier or statutory provision
(b)	Stabilising attendance and engagement in school
(c)	Addressing early-stage SEMH and EBSA concerns
(d)	Supporting emotional regulation and resilience through targeted interventions
(e)	Enhancing family engagement and collaboration with schools
(f)	Strengthening inclusion practices within mainstream settings
(g)	Pupils who are still on roll at mainstream schools but require additional support to maintain engagement

(e)	Require interim education while awaiting placement

tender.description:
Royal Berkshire Fire and Rescue Service (RBFRS) currently employ approximately 65 staff who regularly or occasionally work alone, and who may be at risk of physical/verbal abuse, accidents, illness or injury. Lone worker equipment is currently supplied to staff, as a means of enabling staff members to quickly raise an alarm if required. When alarms are raised, they are monitored by an alarm receiving centre (ARC) which is staffed 24/7/365. They will initiate the escalation process.  It is imperative that issues are resolved within the formally agreed timescales. The need for lone worker equipment is determined by the Head of Service responsible for health and safety, via the risk assessment process. The supply of equipment is managed through the Health and Safety Team with individual team managers monitoring usage and managing the escalation contacts for their teams. The range of equipment currently in use is either a stand-alone device or a mobile phone app. The current requirement for approximately 65 users, with the flexibility to increase provision up to 85 users during the Contract Period, subject to orders being placed as and when required.
RBFRS has a requirement for the provision of a third party 24/7/365 monitored lone worker solution which could be either a mobile phone application, a stand-alone device, or a combination of the two, that allow alarms to be raised either discreetly or overtly and appropriate intervention and/or escalation to be made as required, in order to minimise any risks that working alone involves. The solution should be discrete, reliable and robust, simple and intuitive to use with minimum training.  A range of devices are needed to allow staff to select their preferred choice, based on their role and type of lone working activities.

tender.description: An 18-month contract for the provision of logistics support, repair, and overhaul services to sustain Land Environment (LE) Tactical Communications and Information Systems (TacCIS) capabilities
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
The current Logistics Support Contract (LSC) is due to expire on 27 February 2027. The contract is scheduled to be replaced by a competitively procured Logistics Support contract. The new contract is not anticipated to be awarded until February 2028 and interim arrangements are required to mitigate a gap in service provision of up to 18 months. 
Failure to place a continuation contract with Babcock will result in a critical capability gap. It will leave MOD without access to a single point in Industry able to coordinate support to the various tactical communications systems and equipment currently deployed by Field Army.  Without support services there is a risk of a decline in TacCIS availability, an inability to replace faulty equipment in operational theatres, and a lack of asset visibility in the supply chain. The result in the battlespace will be a loss of information exchange capabilities and an unacceptable risk to safety and life.
The lack of logistics services will also impact the BCIP 5.7 update, removing the underpinning logistical support chain that provides the facility to transition from the current BCIP 5.6 capability and preventing the work required to ensure in-service equipment is at the right standard to be updated.

tender.description:
We intend to make a direct award for the provision of a housing‑focused discount and rewards application that enables residents to access discounts, offers, and cost‑saving opportunities, and supports the application of rewards, credits, or incentives directly to rent accounts. A direct award is justified under the Procurement Act 2023 on the basis that the required service is only available from a single supplier capable of delivering a fully integrated housing‑specific rewards platform with the necessary functionality, including rent‑account crediting, housing‑sector integrations, and resident engagement tools. 
Awarding the contract directly ensures continuity of service, avoids disproportionate procurement costs, and enables timely delivery of resident cost‑of‑living support and engagement benefits. 
A Transparency Notice will be published on the Central Digital Platform, initiating an 8‑working‑day standstill period in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023.

tender.title: CO6190 - Fabrication of Whitechapel of Market Stalls
tender.description: This work forms part of the Whitechapel Road Improvement Programme (WRIP) which continues to see significant investment in the public spaces around Whitechapel, market, and associated infrastructure, to create the best possible environment for local communities. A market stall prototype has been trialled on Whitechapel Road’s northern footway successfully for several months, and feedback collected from a large range of stakeholders (including the traders themselves) has informed the final design/functionality of the market stall design. This will have a positive impact on the market for all – it will be easier for the Markets Team to manage, it will be a better environment for market traders to sell their products, and it will provide a more spacious, clean and attractive shopping destination for marketgoers. There will be disruption to the public realm and market pitches on the northern footway of Whitechapel Road as the new stalls are installed. Delivery will take place in phases to ensure traders can be relocated to other areas of the market and not disrupt their ability to trade. The production and installation of these market stalls is specialised, technical work. It is expected that the full period of fabrication to installation could take up to 9months.
